summary: Kootenai National Forest tower near Noxon, Sanders County, Montana; built 1930-31, lookouts named into 1942, abandoned 1950, now gone.

facts.status_note: Gone. Abandoned in 1950; no source describes what remains.

staffing.status: lookouts named in newspaper notices, 1930 to 1942

events.note: Sanders County paper says the cabin and lookout tower were completed by June 1930; firelookout.com dates the tower to 1931
William Scholes of Noxon assigned the lookout post; first lookout named in the sources
Earl Helms set to be stationed there that summer (June 1933 notice)
Frank Hoag called lookout on Gov. Peak (July 1942 notice)

evidence.supports: cabin 1930, tower built 1931, 50-foot pole L-4 tower, abandoned 1950
evidence.quote: Established with a cabin in 1930, this 50' pole L-4 tower, built in 1931, was abandoned in 1950.

evidence.supports: about three miles northeast of Noxon
R.I.P. label with 1931 start date and open end
cabin and lookout tower completed, June 1930, Government Peak
evidence.quote: A new fireman cabin and lookout tower has been completed on Government Peak in the Rock Creek country.

evidence.supports: page files notices under Government Mountain

evidence.quote: William Scholes of Noxon has been assigned the position of lookout at this place
Earl Helms will be lookout on Government Peak.

evidence.supports: Earl Helms set to be stationed there for summer 1933
evidence.quote: Earl Helms left Tuesday for Noxon, from where he left for Government Peak to be stationed as a lookout this summer.
Earl Helms who has been a lookout on Government peak is home now.

notes_for_editor: Build year disputed. The June 1930 newspaper item (cite 2) says the cabin and tower were completed; firelookout.com (cite 1) dates the tower to 1931 and the cabin to 1930. The built event uses 1930 from the newspaper; change it to 1931 if an editor prefers the page. Location conflict is still open. The record point (48.04148, -115.78897) matches the FFLA list; the other coordinates in the brief (west_us_lookouts, 48.0313, -115.7261) come from a source not read here, and no source read gives coordinates for the lookout itself. height_m 15.2 treats the 50 ft as tower height; firelookout.com does not say whether that is tower or cab height. Staffing names come from newspaper items as quoted on the Forest Lookouts page; the newspapers themselves were not checked. The 1950 abandonment rests on firelookout.com alone. Nothing read covers fires, access or present-day condition. No photos added.
